items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: This was [the] most, you know, fun... It was Ikoma and his band... I got a job... Mister Ikoma‟s band got a job there... I had to back up on piano.

ctx.x: I think it was [19]48, uh, it was summer. And, uh, I was a little bit, I was a little bit, kinda, trying to play, improvise and so on and so on, you know. When I went to … Mister Yamada, he was an old man, I mean an old-timer. There were a few old timers, Japanese old times, who used to play on the boats. I think, one of the most important, probably the one was [trumpeter] Mister Fumio Nanri, because [they] had a Nanri award set up by Swing Journal. I‟m the first recipient. But, that was a long time ago [1975]….…
blah, so on and so on. Juggler was just, “We want the tempo about like that” or something, and we just had to…. This was [the] most, you know, fun.
